scope: Everything: build knowledge, product evidence chain, and domain research context.

Source.desc: external evidence we did not produce

Finding.desc: a measured fact drawn from a Source

Constraint.desc: a rule that binds the build

Decision.desc: a choice made, with its reasoning

Competitor.desc: an existing service we are measured against

BuildNode.desc: mirror of a build_graph node, so the two graphs link without merging

Failure.desc: a gate or verifier rejection, kept even after it was fixed

Deviation.desc: where implementation diverged from spec, and why

Anchor.desc: a measurement from OUTSIDE the graph; the only thing that verifies a claim

Document.desc: a specification or planning document; the written form of a constraint or decision

Repository.desc: the git remote this build is committed to

rules: An edge is invalid unless its endpoints match the relation's domain and range.
Every edge carries `at` and `by`. A bare connection is not a fact.
Nothing is ever deleted. Supersede it, so the history stays auditable.
Only an Anchor or a Verification may verify a Claim. Self-assertion is not verification.

The canonical PersistedSession omitted armedHourBand while the frozen-band rules depend on it. A session recovered after a frozen tab would have silently rescheduled on the current band instead of the band it armed under. A correctness bug, not a naming one: the prose named the field, the canonical block did not declare it.
Where the prose in STATE_MACHINE.md and its canonical TypeScript block disagree, the block wins, and that rule is now stated in the file. The two had drifted apart silently.

CandidateModeTest becomes dwellEvaluator.test.ts. The dwell proof rules (5 fixes, 60 s span, 100 m accuracy gate, outside-reset) survive unchanged; the background service that hosted them does not. Dwell evidence is discarded on any watch interruption, never resumed.
Deadlines are absolute epoch millis, never performance.now(). Monotonic time does not survive a frozen tab, which is the normal case on web, not the edge case.

After three consecutive blockers of the same class (pivot residue in a doc a node reads), swept every document in the remaining nodes' reads arrays instead of waiting for the fourth. Eight genuine sites fixed across DATA_MODEL, RESPONSIVE_SPEC, STATES_CATALOGUE, INTERACTION_SPEC, MAP_SPEC, COPY, BUSINESS_RULES, SETUP and SECRETS_AND_ACCESS.

DATA_MODEL.md carried Kotlin data classes inside typescript fences, which is why the type checker read them without complaint. Reconciled to the models T2.1 actually produced and verified, rather than writing a second contract for the same types. Where a node has already built and passed its verifiers, the spec is corrected to match the code.

The first pivot sweep matched Android keywords, so it could not see Kotlin syntax inside typescript fences, mangled identifiers whose case broke the pattern (org.Leaflet:Leaflet-android), or self-contradictions made of valid words (RESPONSIVE_SPEC said use px for all text, never px for type). A keyword grep cannot find a contradiction. The second pass matched syntax and API shapes instead and found 33 lines across 10 files.

The MAP_SPEC cache row was rewritten without reading the surrounding prose, leaving the file saying both no tile-cache cap and 64 MB. Self-inflicted during the first sweep: a row was patched in isolation.

DATA_MODEL.md carried a second contract for the persisted session, in Room column terms, omitting armedHourBand and deadlineEpochMs. It contradicted PersistedSession, and it was the one T4.1 had to write to. Now declared as exactly PersistedSession plus one local history field, with the interface named as the winner on any future disagreement.

INTERACTION_SPEC claimed a web audio element plays through silent and Do Not Disturb. It does not, on any browser, and there is no API to override either. A false capability claim that would have reached the submission write-up.

Where the web cannot do what the iOS product does, the spec states the limit in the same place it used to state the capability: no silent-switch override, no lock-screen presentation, no turning the screen on, no undismissable notification, no FLAG_SECURE, no background arming, and navigator.vibrate absent entirely on iOS Safari. Disclosed rather than implied, in the UI and the write-up.

The Firebase Web app registration moves from T8.2 to a human gate before T1.2. The whole product is a web app, so the web SDK performs anonymous auth at T1.2; deferring it to the console node was four nodes too late. One registration serves both app and console.

There is exactly one Service Worker and it exists only because Chrome on Android has no Notification constructor: new Notification() throws there and ServiceWorkerRegistration.showNotification is the only route. It has no fetch handler and caches nothing. Codex recommended removing the Service Worker entirely, which would have silenced check-ins on the primary target platform. Consequences accepted and written down: no offline first launch, no tile cache, and offline means the page is already open when connectivity drops.

BUILD_CONFIG said a Service Worker caches static assets, ARCHITECTURE forbade a Service Worker, MAP_SPEC required a 64 MB tile cache and CODEX_TASKS required offline zone rendering. Four documents, no two compatible. Resolved into one canonical statement in WEB_PLATFORM.md that the others now cite.

Two rounds of fixes patched individual rows without reading the surrounding file, which produced new defects rather than fewer: MAP_SPEC asserted both no cache cap and 64 MB in the same file, and a COMPONENT_LIBRARY replacement left the fragment 'Never log, never screenshot: set'. Method changed to reading each file end to end before editing it.

The pivot updated English copy and left the Telugu column describing Android. warn_battery_title read 'Saaya only watches while this page is open' in English and 'Android can stop Saaya in the background' in Telugu. Half the intended users read only the stale half.

Manual entry only, no contact picker. SECRETS_AND_ACCESS states contacts access is never requested and its absence is verifiable in devtools, which is part of the privacy argument; the Contact Picker API is also Chrome-Android-only, so it would work for some users and vanish for others.

Measured from the frozen asset, not reasoned about: 126 of 165 polygon vertices lie outside their own declared geofence_radius_m, across 23 of the 24 zones. Worst is bheemili_police_station at 21,535 m from its centroid against a declared 2,000 m. Verified independently with Haversine against public/assets/vizag_heatmap.geojson, which is byte-identical to the two other copies. Separately confirmed: all 24 declared centroids DO fall inside their own polygons, so centroid-anchored map labels are sound, and a bounding-box prefilter admits 165 of 165 vertices.

Three documents specified geofence_radius_m as the containment prefilter. It is a legacy Android Geofencing parameter, which could only register circles, and it was never an approximation of polygon extent. Because a boundary point counts as inside, using it would have refused to arm across most of Vizag: a silent false negative in the one path that must not have one. Codex found it at T4.2 by measuring the asset rather than trusting the spec.

The containment prefilter is each polygon's bounding box, computed once at load from the frozen asset. Provably contains every point of its polygon, two comparisons per axis. geofence_radius_m stays in the asset because the asset is frozen and audited, and nothing reads it. The general rule is now stated in BUSINESS_RULES: a prefilter may return extra candidates and may never exclude a point the polygon would accept.

Motion is CSS transitions with cubic-bezier curves plus a global prefers-reduced-motion rule. No JS spring solver and no animation library. The curves are DERIVED from the frozen physics rather than replacing it: each curve's first-peak overshoot is matched to the damping ratio it comes from, so motion.spring.damping stays the source of truth and a retune starts there.

The recommended spring curve cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1) was measured at 9.78% first-peak overshoot against the 2.84% implied by the frozen dampingRatio 0.75: three and a half times the specified bounce. It is the common springy preset and would have passed review by feel. Replaced with cubic-bezier(0.34,1.3,0.64,1), measured 2.99%. The founder direction is warm and springy, not bouncy, and an emergency surface that visibly wobbles reads as a toy.

Fonts are downloaded once, subset with pyftsubset, and committed to public/fonts with their licence files. The build never fetches a font. Same reasoning that chose Leaflet and CARTO over Google Maps: nothing may depend on a third party being reachable on submission day. This rules out next/font/google, which downloads at build time and cannot subset Material Symbols by icon name. Upstream files are pinned by recorded sha256 rather than by a commit id.

Subsetting Noto Sans Telugu must retain the akhn, blwf, half, pres, abvs, blws and psts layout features. Dropping them silently breaks conjunct formation, which nobody testing in English would notice, and Telugu is half the intended audience.

The font sourcing table sent Material Symbols Rounded to google/fonts, where ofl/materialsymbolsrounded returns 404. Written from memory in the same commit that told Codex to pin sources by hash for reproducibility. It also implied OFL for a family COMPLIANCE.md correctly records as Apache 2.0. Corrected to google/material-design-icons/variablefont, which is also the only place the matching .codepoints file exists, and that file is what makes subsetting by icon possible.

All four upstream paths checked against the live GitHub API on 2026-08-24, not recalled: google/fonts ofl/poppins (static TTFs, OFL.txt present); google/fonts ofl/notosanstelugu (NotoSansTelugu[wdth,wght].ttf, TWO axes not one, OFL.txt present); google/material-design-icons variablefont/ (MaterialSymbolsRounded[FILL,GRAD,opsz,wght].ttf and matching .codepoints); google/material-design-icons root LICENSE.

External source paths, filenames and versions written into the spec are verified against the live source before they are frozen, not recalled. A spec that tells the builder to pin by hash while itself carrying an unverified path is asking for a rigour it does not practise.
